spec.name: Module 9 — Raw Concrete Housing Block
spec.description: A tall brutalist housing block on heavy pilotis, stacked concrete floor bands with deep window recesses, cantilevered balconies on the front face, a taller service core at the rear and a working rooftop plant deck.
spec.layout: The block faces +Z. Ground level (y 0–2.6) is open: a grid of thick square concrete pilotis carries everything, with a recessed dark glazed lobby box set back at z -1.5..0.5, a deep cast canopy slab over the entry on the +Z side, low concrete planter walls and a rusted metal door — this part rests on y = 0. From 2.6 to 9.0 the main shaft rises as five stacked concrete floor bands (each 1.28 m), each band a slightly different concrete tone, punched with deep vertical window recesses: dark glass set 0.25 m back, separated by broad concrete piers, with two rows of narrow slit windows near the flanks. The front (+Z) face carries cantilevered balcony slabs at each floor line, projecting 1.2 m, with low concrete upstand walls and dark metal railings. At the rear (z -3.8..-2.2), offset toward +X, a bare service core of sheer board-marked concrete rises through and 4.2 m past the shaft to y 13.2, with a column of small stair windows, a stack of dark louvre openings and horizontal formwork board lines. On the shaft roof (y 9.0) sits the roofscape: a tall parapet, a clustered plant enclosure in darker concrete, round vent stacks, a tarred water tank on short legs and a thin antenna mast to y 14.4 — the model's highest point. The style is raw concrete everywhere: flat unrelieved masses, deep shadow in every recess, weathering streaks read as darker concrete pieces under sills and edges, board-form seam lines as thin inset slats, and colour used only sparingly (rusted door, dark glass, one mustard service door, moss on north-facing planters).

Six to eight thick square concrete pilotis (about 0.45 m across, built as stacked frustum boxes or chunky boxes with slightly battered sides) in concreteMid with concreteDark bases, standing on low pad footings that touch y = 0. A recessed lobby volume set back to z -1.5..0.5 between two columns: a box of dark glassDark panels with thin concreteDark mullions, a recessBlack doorway opening and the doorRust door with a small round handle. A deep cast canopy slab (concreteLight, 0.3 m thick, cantilevering to z 2.6) over the entry, carried on two of the pilotis, with a boardSeam line of thin inset slats on its soffit. Around the perimeter: low concrete planter walls (concreteDark, 0.55 m high) holding planterSoil with a few blocky mossGreen shrubs, and a concreteDark ground slab whose top surface is the podium floor. One mustard doorService side door on the -X flank. Everything sits inside the box, columns and footings on y = 0.
parts.attaches: Its top face is exactly the podiumTop plane at y 2.6 across the full footprint; the shaft and serviceCore start there. Shares the footprint edges x ±2.7, z ±3.5 with the parts above.

Built as five stacked floor bands, each 1.28 m tall, each a frustumBox or box slab in a slightly different concrete tone cycling concreteLight, concreteMid, concreteDark so the stacking reads, with a thin concreteShadow shadow gap line between bands. Each band is punched on the +Z front face with deep vertical window recesses: recesses built as recessBlack inset boxes set 0.25 m back, each holding a glassDark or glassTeal window pane part with thin railingMetal frames, separated by broad 0.5 m concrete piers. parts.builds: The cantilevered balcony stack on the front face. Five balcony slabs (concreteLight, 0.18 m thick, 5.6 m wide, projecting from z 3.5 to z 4.6), one at each floor line: tops at y 3.9, 5.18, 6.46, 7.74 and the parapet-line slab at 8.9. Each slab has a visible fascia edge band in concreteMid with a boardSeam thin seam. On each slab: a low concrete upstand wall (concreteMid, 0.35 m) along the outer edge and short returns, and above it a dark railingMetal balustrade built from thin vertical balusters (0.03 m square, about 14 per balcony) with a top handrail rail in railingHighlight and a bottom rail — all small parts seated on the slab. Under each slab nose, two short angled concreteDark corbel brackets tying back to the facade. On two balconies, small human touches: a glassTeal privacy screen panel, a planter box with mossGreen shrubs, a folded deckchair shape in doorRust canvas. A vertical drainage streak of concreteWeathered runs down the facade below each slab's corner drain.

A sheer board-marked concrete tower from y 2.6 to 13.2, footprint x -1.6..1.9, z -3.8..-2.3, in concreteDark with strong horizontal formwork: repeated thin boardSeam slat strips 0.4 m apart wrapping all four faces, and a few concreteWeathered panels where the pour varied. A single column of small stair windows runs up the +Z face of the core: pairs of small glassDark panes with concreteLight surrounds at each level, deeply recessed in recessBlack boxes. The core reads as unrelieved mass: almost no openings, deep shadow, board lines only.
